item.title: Building a Production SEO Agent Stack with Claude Code: claude-seo Architecture Deep Dive
item.guid: title:building a production seo agent stack with claude code claude seo architecture deep dive
item.description: Context: Why Another SEO Tool When We Have Screaming Frog? When evaluating AgriciDaniel/claude-seo for integration into our content automation pipeline, the first question was obvious: why not just shell out to existing headless scrapers or commercial SEO APIs? The repository claims 26 sub-skills and 19 sub-agents covering technical audits, E-E-A-T scoring, schema validation, and agent-readiness checks (Lighthouse Agentic Browsing, WebMCP, llms. txt). The value proposition centers on native LLM context awareness —not just crawling sites, but reasoning about discoverability through the lens of emerging agentic browsing protocols. The operational question: does this actually reduce token waste and improve output quality compared to feeding raw HTML dumps into Claude, or is it architectural overhead?

item.guid: title:the rise of ai orchestration connecting intelligence with real world execution
item.description: Why intelligent models still struggle to execute real-world tasks — and how orchestration connects LLMs, tools, memory, and workflows to make AI systems work. The Rise of AI Orchestration, with an orchestrator hub linked to LLM, tools, memory and APIs The Assistant That Knew Everything and Did Nothing Picture a Monday morning. You type one sentence to your AI assistant: “Pull last quarter’s top five customer complaints, draft a fix plan, and book a review with the team. ” The reply arrives in seconds. It is a flawless essay on how to analyze customer complaints: clear headings, confident tone, even a tidy checklist. And not one complaint was read.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: Some “coherence arguments” are two different things in a trenchcoat
item.guid: title:some coherence arguments are two different things in a trenchcoat
item.description: The “two kids in a trenchcoat” trope , in case you haven’t heard of it. Image sources: 1 , 2 tl;dr I go through three “coherence arguments”, related to (1) market competition, (2) AI self-reflection and self-modification, and (3) AI training algorithms. I argue that each of these implies a pressure for (something like) “being self-consistent”, and also a pressure for (something like) “only caring about long-term eventual outcomes, with ruthless indifference to anything else”. But the latter pressure tends to be weaker and/or more contingent than the former. So it's bad to lump them together and call them by the same name. 1.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k2 5 visual agentic intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K2. 5, the most powerful open-source model to date. Kimi K2. 5 builds on Kimi K2 with continued pretraining over approximately 15T mixed visual and text tokens. Built as a native multimodal model, K2. 5 delivers state-of-the-art coding and vision capabilities and a self-directed agent swarm paradigm.

item.title: The Interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety. They seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build.
item.guid: title:the interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for ai safety they seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build
item.description: It’s hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them. Our goal is to be able to explain large language models’ behavior, and to use that understanding to identify problems that are hard to see from the outside, such as situations where a model’s stated reasoning differs from what it’s actually doing. Our early work focused on mapping the internal mechanisms of AI models. Today, we increasingly apply our methods to real models to understand how they think and why they behave the way they do. We’ve developed techniques that allow us to understand models’ inner workings in plain language, making it easier to detect unsafe behavior or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it. Interpretability
